attributes.body_ja:
「に決（き）まっている」は、確証（かくしょう）はなくても (A) だと強（つよ）く思（おも）っているときや、または (A) であることが当然（とうぜん）だと信（しん）じているときに使（つか）われる強（つよ）い断定（だんてい）の表現（ひょうげん）です。これは「に」と五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「決（き）まる」のテイル形（けい）の組（く）み合（あ）わせで、「きっと (A) だ」や「絶対（ぜったい）に (A) だ」というような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

「に決（き）まっている」は動詞（どうし）、イ形容詞（けいようし）、ナ形容詞（けいようし）、または名詞（めいし）の後（あと）に直接（ちょくせつ）付（つ）きます。

「に決（き）まっている」は (A) に関（かん）する話（はな）し手（て）の主観的（しゅかんてき）な意見（いけん）を表（あらわ）す表現（ひょうげん）です。事実（じじつ）かどうかに関（かか）わらず、話（はな）し手（て）がもともと持（も）っている考（かんが）えや思（おも）い込（こ）みに基（もと）づいて「(A) に違（ちが）いない」と一方的（いっぽうてき）に断定（だんてい）するときに使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
に決（き）まっている is a strong expression which indicates that (A) is something that the speaker either strongly believes to be true (but cannot confirm), or that they believe that (A) is only natural. These meanings primarily end up being translated as 'surely (A)', 'bound to be (A)', or 'certainly (A)'. As this structure is a combination of に and the ている-form of the う-Verb 決（き）まる 'to be decided', the closest literal translation is 'for (A) to be decisively the case'.

に決（き）まっている may appear directly following verbs, い-Adjectives, な-Adjectives or nouns.

に決（き）まっている primarily focuses on the speaker's subjective opinion about (A). This means that it takes into consideration their own preformed opinions or thoughts about (A), regardless of what the actual facts may be.

確かに and に決まっている both express a strong degree of certainty, but differ in usage and nuance. 確かに is often used to concede or acknowledge something as true, and can at times be followed by a contrast, as in 確かに高いが、品質もいい (It’s certainly expensive, but the quality is good). に決まっている conveys confident personal judgment or obviousness, as in 彼がやったに決まっている (He definitely did it).3

second_relatable.title: に決まっている
second_relatable.meaning: Surely, Bound to, Certainly, Be decided

attributes.body: Both にする and に決まっている relate to decisions but differ in use. にする expresses making a choice, often in daily contexts like picking what to eat, similar to 'I'll go with X.' に決まっている, despite using 決まる, often just shows strong belief, meaning 'It's surely X' or 'It's bound to be X,' rather than an actual decision.

first_relatable.title: にする
first_relatable.meaning: To decide on, To choose, To make something into, To view something as

second_relatable.title: に決まっている
second_relatable.meaning: Surely, Bound to, Certainly, Be decided

attributes.body: に違いない and に決まっている both express strong conviction, but differ in tone and basis of judgment. に違いない implies a strong conclusion drawn from evidence or context, e.g. '何かあったに違いない' ('Something must have happened'). に決まっている conveys more assertive confidence, often based on common sense or the obvious, e.g. '美味しいに決まっている' ('Of course it tastes good').

first_relatable.title: に違いない
first_relatable.meaning: There is no doubt that, I'm sure

second_relatable.title: に決まっている
second_relatable.meaning: Surely, Bound to, Certainly, Be decided

attributes.body: These patterns are related in that both center around the idea of something being decided. ことになる expresses that something has been decided or will happen, often beyond the speaker's control, e.g. 転勤することになった ('It's been decided that I'll be transferred'), while に決まっている expresses that something is decisively true, e.g. 勝つに決まっている ('They'll definitely win').
